title: Google Review NFC Tabletop Prompts — Acrylic Stands / Tent Cards / Bill Presenters with NTAG213
summary: Use this page when the review prompt is meant to sit on a table, counter surface or waiting-area stand and the goal is to make it visible enough to drive taps or scans without staff explaining every time. Covers acrylic table-tent stands, bill-presenter inserts, host-stand counter cards and check-presenter NFC tent cards (NTAG213 + QR fallback) for restaurants, cafes, bars, hotel lounges, salon waiting areas and clinic reception desks — operated within FTC 16 CFR Part 465 + Google Business Profile review policy frameworks (no review-gating, no incentivised reviews, 'leave us a review' copy).
heroPoints: Tabletop prompts depend on placement, design clarity and how obvious the action feels without staff help.
Acrylic cards, mini stands and sticker-backed prompts each solve different surface and visibility problems.
The first pilot should test where customers naturally notice and act on the prompt, not just where the team wants it to sit.

brief.label: Tabletop placement form-factor library
items: Acrylic table-tent stand — clear acrylic A-frame with NFC card inserted; restaurant + bar standard.
Acrylic block stand — solid acrylic block with NFC card embedded; salon + spa upmarket finish.
Bill-presenter NFC insert — NFC card slipped into check-presenter for end-of-meal prompt.
Host-stand counter card — vertical NFC card stand at hostess / front-desk position.
Tabletop tent card (printed cardstock with embedded inlay) — disposable tent card for events / pop-ups.
Wood-veneer tent stand — premium FSC bamboo / walnut for boutique / luxury hospitality.
Counter sticker — peel-and-stick NFC + QR sticker on smooth surface (counter / glass / acrylic).
Magnetic backplate version — refrigerator / metal-surface mountable for office / clinic break rooms.

brief.label: Vertical-specific placement strategy
items: Restaurants — table-tent on each table or bill-presenter at end of meal; peak satisfaction = post-dessert / pre-payment.
Cafes + bars — counter-top at register + table-tent at seated areas; peak satisfaction = at-pickup / mid-drink.
Hotel lounges + lobbies — coffee-table tent + concierge-desk counter card; peak satisfaction = check-out morning.
Salons + spas — at-station tent (visible during service) + check-out counter card; peak satisfaction = end-of-service.
Clinics + medical offices — waiting-room side table + appointment-desk counter card; peak satisfaction = post-appointment.
Dental practices — chairside counter card + check-out tent; peak satisfaction = at-checkout.
Auto dealerships + service — service-bay waiting-area tent + check-out counter card.
Veterinary practices — exam-room side table + check-out counter card.

brief.label: Chip + memory + form factor
items: NTAG213 (144 B) — baseline; rewritable URL; 90% of programme volume.
NTAG215 (504 B) — premium variant for cards with vCard + review URL hybrid.
QR fallback — printed alongside NFC for older phones / non-NFC users.
Acrylic 4-mm clear stand — laser-cut, polished edges, 80×120 mm typical insert size.
Wood veneer 6-mm — laser-engraved branding + slot for NFC card insert.
Bill-presenter slot insert — sized to standard 90×54 mm credit-card slot.
Counter card 80×140 mm portrait — vertical with embedded weighted base.
Magnetic backplate option — for break-room / kitchen / office surface mounting.

brief.label: Copy + design framework
items: Headline: 'Loved your visit? Tap here to leave a review' — never 'Leave us 5 stars'.
Brand colours + logo + Google logo + star graphic.
QR code printed below NFC tap zone — ≥15 mm × 15 mm with 4 mm quiet zone (ISO/IEC 18004).
Tap zone marker: 'Tap your phone here' arrow + Apple / Android compatibility note.
Multi-language overlays for international hospitality (EN / FR / ES / DE / ZH / JA).
Avoid pressure language; respect customer choice.
Brand-standard locked: BU customisation gated through brand approval.
Multi-location: per-location encoded URL; centrally controlled design template.

brief.label: FTC + Google compliance framework
items: FTC 16 CFR Part 465 (effective Oct 21, 2024) — rule against fake / AI-generated / insider / paid-positive reviews.
FTC Endorsement Guides — material-connection disclosure for incentivised reviews.
Google Business Profile review policy — no review-gating (only-positive customers asked).
Card copy: 'Leave us a review' — NEVER 'Leave us a 5-star review'.
Cards offered to ALL customers — not selectively to satisfied only.
No incentivisation: no discount + no entry-to-prize-draw + no free item for review.
EU Digital Services Act — review-source transparency obligations for EU operators.
ACCC (AU) + CMA (UK) — equivalent fake-review prohibitions.

brief.label: Programme economics + ROI
items: Per-stand BOM: $5–$15 acrylic stand + NFC card combined; $3–$8 sticker; $15–$40 wood-veneer.
Per-location cost: typically $50–$300 depending on number of stands per location (5–20 stands).
Review-velocity uplift: 30–60% increase via passive tabletop placement (lower than counter-handoff but still meaningful).
Multi-location estate: $5K–$50K initial deployment for 100–1000 location chain.
Reorder cycle: 12–18 months typical; brand-refresh trigger or new-location rollout.
Replacement reserve: 5–10% per year for damaged / lost stands (higher than counter cards due to handling).
Supplementary to counter-handoff: tabletop is a passive layer; combine with active staff-prompt for max conversion.
ROI compared to paid review platforms: 70–80% lower per-review acquisition cost.

brief.label: Operations + lifecycle
items: Daily wipe-down compatible: choose materials that survive cleaning chemistry.
Theft / loss replacement: weighted base + magnetic backplate reduces accidental movement.
Damage-resistance: acrylic survives normal handling; wood-veneer scratches over time.
Multi-location resupply: shipped pre-sorted by location with location-specific URLs encoded.
Off-cycle replacement: damaged stand returned for refurb / chip transfer to new stand.
Brand refresh: 12–18 month design + URL refresh aligned with brand-standard book update.
Per-stand analytics: GBP review velocity per location; harder to attribute to specific table without per-table encoding.
Per-table encoding (advanced): each table gets unique sub-URL for table-level conversion analytics.

brief.label: Implementation programme stages
items: Stage 1 — GBP audit + per-location review-link capture.
Stage 2 — Vertical-specific placement strategy + form factor decision per surface.
Stage 3 — Stand BOM + chip + design + copy lock-in.
Stage 4 — FTC + Google compliance review + brand-standard sign-off.
Stage 5 — Production + per-location encoding + assembly.
Stage 6 — Despatch + on-site staff training + soft-launch one location.
Stage 7 — Full estate rollout + GBP velocity tracking.
Stage 8 — Quarterly placement audit + reorder cycle + analytics review.

dataHighlight.heading: Tabletop placement uplift atop counter-card baseline
dataHighlight.text: Tabletop NFC review prompts (acrylic table-tent stands, bill-presenter inserts, host-stand counter cards, wood-veneer tent stands) deliver 30–60 % review-velocity uplift as a passive layer atop active counter-card handoff — combining to drive 60–90 % combined uplift vs verbal-only baselines in restaurants, cafes, hotel lounges, salons + spas, clinics, dental practices, auto-dealership service-bays and veterinary practices. Per-stand BOM ranges $5–$15 acrylic + NFC card combined, $3–$8 sticker, $15–$40 wood-veneer; per-location cost typically $50–$300 for 5–20 stands per location. Compliance framework: FTC 16 CFR Part 465 + FTC Endorsement Guides + Google Business Profile review policy + EU Digital Services Act + ACCC + CMA — all enforce no review-gating, no incentivisation, 'leave us a review' (not '5-star review') copy. Tabletop format library spans 8 vertical-specific placements: restaurant table-tent + bill-presenter (peak post-dessert / pre-payment), cafe + bar counter-top + table tent, hotel lounge coffee-table + concierge-desk, salon at-station + check-out counter, clinic waiting-room + appointment-desk, dental chairside + check-out, auto-service-bay waiting-area, vet exam-room + check-out.

items.label: Week 1 — GBP audit + vertical-specific placement plan
items.text: Verify Google Business Profile claimed + verified per location. Generate short review URL per location. Map physical placements per location: counter card + table-tent + bill-presenter + waiting-room tent. Decide passive-only vs hybrid (passive + active staff handoff).

items.label: Week 2 — Stand form factor + chip + design lock-in
items.text: Form factor: acrylic table-tent vs wood-veneer vs bill-presenter slot vs counter sticker. Chip: NTAG213 baseline. Design: brand colours + 'Loved your visit? Tap to leave a review' headline + Google logo + star graphic + QR fallback below NFC zone.

items.label: Week 3 — FTC + Google policy compliance review
items.text: Validate copy: no '5-star' language, no review-gating, no incentivisation. Confirm 'leave us a review' standard. Sign off legal + brand teams. Lock multi-language overlays if international.

items.label: Week 4 — Production + per-location encoding + assembly
items.text: Production wave on confirmed chip + design + form factor. Each NFC card encoded with location-specific GBP URL. Acrylic / wood stand assembled with NFC card insert. Pre-sorted shipping by location.

items.label: Week 5–6 — Despatch + on-site placement + soft-launch
items.text: Distribute to locations. Staff training on placement consistency + cleaning protocol. Soft-launch one location; monitor placement persistence + customer interaction observation.

items.label: Month 2 — Full rollout + per-location GBP velocity tracking
items.text: Full estate rollout. Track per-location review velocity in GBP analytics. Identify high-performing placements vs underperforming. Adjust placement / copy / form factor based on data.

items.label: Month 3–6 — Optimise + reorder + brand refresh
items.text: Quarterly placement audit. Replace damaged / lost stands (5–10% per year baseline). Reorder cycle synced to brand-refresh trigger (12–18 month). Per-location placement standardisation.

items.label: Year 2+ — Operate + scale + cross-vertical learning
items.text: Vertical context spans hospitality, healthcare, salon-spa, fitness, retail and home-services programmes — each estate carries its own placement-pattern library + reorder cycle + FTC compliance audit cadence. Multi-location estate scale-up + per-location placement governance + per-staff prompt KPI integration into manager scorecards + cross-vertical placement-best-practice sharing.

sections.title: Tabletop tent architecture — form factor, materials, footprint, visibility
bullets: Bi-fold A-frame tent — most common form factor; 6×4×6 in (15×10×15 cm) folded paper / cardstock with NFC chip embedded; freestanding on flat surface; 2-3 minute hand-assembly per piece; $0.30-$1.00 per unit at 1K+ qty.
Tri-fold prism tent — 3-sided prism / triangular; visible from all sides; ideal for round tables + central placement; $0.40-$1.20 per unit.

Tabletop stand with insert pocket — reusable lucite / acrylic / wood holder with replaceable paper / card insert; reusable + cleaning-resistant + premium feel; $3-$15 per stand + $0.20 per refresh insert.
Counter-block + lucite — small acrylic block (3×3×3 in / 7.5×7.5×7.5 cm) with NFC chip embedded in top + 'Tap to Review' engraving; durable + minimalist; $5-$20 per piece.
Engraved wooden block — premium-tier for restaurant / spa / coffee shop with sustainability emphasis; FSC-certified hardwood + laser-engraved logo + 'Tap to Review' + NFC chip; $8-$30 per piece.
Metal tabletop sign — luxury restaurant + premium spa / coffee shop; brass / brushed steel / aluminum sign with NFC chip + brand logo; $15-$50 per piece.

Window decal + countertop sticker — for venues without tabletop space (counter-only fast-casual, bar height table, cafe banco); peel-and-stick NFC sticker on tabletop or window surface; $0.30-$0.80 per piece.
Footprint considerations — tabletop tent occupies 6×4×6 in × N tables; restaurant with 20-50 tables = 20-50 tents; multi-location chain × 50-500 locations = 1K-25K tents in deployment.
Visibility hierarchy — at-eye-level when seated (best); 45-degree angle when standing (acceptable); flat on table (lowest visibility); freestanding A-frame outperforms flat by 3-5× tap-rate.

Lighting — restaurant typically dim (50-200 lux); high-contrast tent design (white background + dark logo + 'Tap to Review' text) catches eye at low light; reflective metallic accent (silver / gold) reinforces visibility.
Cleaning + sanitization — tent surfaces wiped down daily / between guests; substrate must withstand sanitizer (alcohol + quaternary ammonium); waterproof + chemical-resistant lamination essential.
Wind + flow resistance — outdoor patio + open-air venue requires weighted base + wind-resistant design; some tents include sandbag base or magnetic table-attachment.
Multi-language design — bilingual + trilingual tent (English + Spanish + French + Mandarin) for diverse-customer venues; flip-side variant or QR code redirects to language-specific landing page.

Brand-cohesive design — tent design language matches venue brand (luxury hotel: gold accent + cream + serif; cafe: pastel + sans-serif; medical: white + blue + clinical sans-serif); reinforces brand experience.

Damage + replacement cycle — restaurant tabletop tent lifecycle 6-18 months (food spillage + handling); spa / clinic 12-24 months (cleaner environment); hotel 12-36 months (low traffic, cleaning-resistant).

sections.title: Placement geometry + customer-flow optimisation
bullets: Restaurant table center — A-frame tent at table center between seated guests; 10-25% sustained tap rate at casual + family-style; visible during entire meal.
Restaurant check-presenter slot — tent integrated with bill-presenter; tap moment at payment; 8-15% conversion at full-service.
Cafe / coffee shop tabletop — A-frame tent on each table or counter; passive but high-frequency exposure; 5-10% conversion (lower than full-service due to fast turnover).
Hotel in-room desk / nightstand — A-frame tent in guest room with 'Share your stay on Google' messaging; multi-day exposure window; 3-10% sustained at premium + boutique.
Hotel lobby seating area — A-frame tent on lobby coffee table; passive prompt during pre-check-in / departure wait; 2-5% conversion.
Spa / salon waiting area — A-frame tent on reading-magazine table / reception coffee table; passive prompt during 5-15 minute wait; 3-8% conversion.
Medical clinic exam room — A-frame tent on exam room counter / patient chair table; HIPAA-compliant generic prompt; 4-10% conversion.
Medical waiting room — A-frame tent on waiting room reading table / magazine rack adjacent; passive during longer waits; 3-8% conversion.
Bar / lounge — A-frame tent on bar top + cocktail table; signature drink card adjacent; 5-12% conversion.
Boutique retail — A-frame tent at fitting room exit + dressing room table; 4-10% conversion.
Home services + B2B office — A-frame tent on conference room table + reception coffee table; visitor + meeting-attendee passive prompt; 3-8% conversion.
Coworking space + library — A-frame tent on member-desk + shared table + member-lounge; passive prompt; 3-8% conversion.
Veterinary clinic exam room — A-frame tent + pet imagery; pet-emotional context drives 5-12% conversion.
Cruise ship cabin / restaurant table — A-frame tent in cabin + on-board restaurant; multi-format tabletop deployment.

High-frequency vs low-frequency exposure — multi-day hotel exposure (10-30 minutes total tent contact) drives different conversion vs single-meal restaurant (20-90 minutes) vs single-visit clinic exam room (5-30 minutes).

bullets: Casual dining tabletop — A-frame tent with 'How was your meal?' + 'Tap to share on Google' + cafe-style typography; daily-wear-tolerant material; replace every 6-12 months.

Dental clinic exam room — patient-comfort imagery (smile-focused) + 'Share your dental experience' tone.
Chiropractic + PT — A-frame tent on patient adjustment table side + 'Share your progress on Google' supportive tone.

Coffee shop — counter A-frame + tabletop tent + Wi-Fi-login redirect to GBP review; 'Loved your coffee?' casual tone.

sections.title: FTC + Google compliance + venue-specific advertising rules
bullets: FTC 16 CFR Part 465 (effective 21 October 2024) — prohibits review-gating + incentivising reviews + AI-generated reviews + suppressing negative reviews; penalty up to $51,744 per violation. Applies to all tabletop prompts regardless of vertical.

Compliant prompt language — 'If you enjoyed your visit, please share on Google' (passive + truthful + non-incentivised + all-customers-asked); avoid 'Loved your meal? Tap for 5 stars' (gating language).
Google Business Profile review policy — prohibits review-gating, incentivisation, fake reviews, off-topic reviews; violation triggers GBP suspension.
Consumer Review Fairness Act (15 U.S.C. § 45b, 2016) — prohibits non-disparagement clauses in form contracts blocking honest reviews.
EU Omnibus Directive 2019/2161 — EU-side anti-fake-review enforcement; up to 4% annual EU turnover penalty.
California Business and Professions Code § 17500 — false advertising; review-related claims must be substantiated.
Multi-state operators — chain operators in 50 states must layer state-specific compliance overlays; lowest-common-denominator language + per-state addendum.

HIPAA Marketing Rule 45 CFR § 164.508 (medical / dental / pharmacy verticals) — tabletop tent must not display PHI; generic 'Share your visit' language qualifies for face-to-face exception + promotional-gift-of-nominal-value exception.
AMA + ADA + specialty-board ethics — medical / dental advertising rules require truthful + non-deceptive + non-coercive language; tabletop tent design + copy must comply.
State medical / dental board rules — California Medical Board, Texas Medical Board, New York State Medical Board + 50-state boards add additional restrictions on review-prompt language.
State cosmetology board (salon + spa + med-spa) — state-by-state restrictions on testimonial use + truthful advertising; per-state compliance audit.
State pharmacy board (pharmacy pickup) — California Board of Pharmacy + Texas + New York + 50-state boards regulate pharmacy advertising.
FAA Federal Aviation Regulations — for hotel + airline lounge cabin tents; standard FTC + airline-specific advertising rules.
State alcohol-control commission (bar + restaurant + liquor pickup) — review prompts subject to state-specific rules.

Cannabis state regulators (dispensary tabletop tent) — California Bureau of Cannabis Control + Colorado MED + Washington WSLCB + state cannabis regulators with varying advertising restrictions; some states prohibit cannabis advertising entirely.
Audit trail — venue should document compliant prompt language + staff training + no-incentive policy + state-specific compliance overlay; defensible in FTC + state board + GBP inquiry.

sections.title: Multi-location + reorder cycle + procurement leverage
bullets: Per-location tabletop tent count — small venue 5-15 tents; mid-size restaurant / spa 20-50 tents; large hotel / coffee chain location 50-200 tents; per-location count drives procurement quantity.
Multi-location chain — 50-5,000 locations × 20-50 tents each = 1K-250K tents at scale; corporate procurement portal + brand-approved supplier list.
Per-location UTM tracking — utm_source=nfc&utm_medium=tabletop&utm_campaign={location-code}; per-location reporting feeds chain-level dashboard.

Brand-standard design — corporate-approved tent colour + logo + URL + brand-tier-appropriate material (cardstock for casual, premium PVC for upmarket, wood / metal for luxury); locations cannot deviate.
Centralised URL management — corporate-managed redirect server resolves utm_campaign={location-code} → GBP placeId; URL changes don't require tent re-printing.
Distribution + replenishment — corporate procurement portal + brand-approved supplier list; per-location quarterly replenishment 50-200 tents + signage; central inventory + just-in-time shipping.
Procurement leverage — corporate bulk procurement (10K-1M+ tents annually) yields $0.15-$0.60 per tent at scale; multi-year + cross-brand contract 10-20% discount.

Brand-refresh trigger — tents align with annual brand refresh; full-estate reorder 12-18 months typical; replacement reserve 5-15% per year for damage / wear / loss / theft (higher in restaurant + bar than spa + clinic).

Sub-stock SKU consolidation — 3-5 strategic tent designs covering 90% of placements (casual A-frame + premium folded card + reusable lucite holder + counter sticker + premium wood/metal); reduces SKU sprawl + procurement complexity.

Reporting + KPI — corporate dashboard shows per-location review velocity + GBP rating + Local Pack ranking + per-tent tap-rate attribution; underperforming placements flagged for design refresh + retraining.
Audit + compliance — quarterly secret-shopper compliance check (tents in place + clean + visible); FTC + state board compliance review annually.
Cross-brand portfolio — multi-brand operator (Marriott, Hilton, Cheesecake Factory, Darden) with cross-brand procurement leverage + per-brand standard design.
Franchise system — franchisor approves tent design + franchisee orders via approved-vendor portal; royalty + co-op marketing fee structure.

Reference deployments — Cava Group, Chipotle, Sweetgreen, Shake Shack, Starbucks (counter sticker), Marriott Bonvoy lobby tents, Hilton Honors lobby tents — all run multi-location NFC tabletop tent programmes at varying scales.
Sustainability — eco-PET + FSC paper + bamboo + recycled-content variants; aligns with operator ESG / CSRD reporting; premium for sustainability-positioned venues.

Replacement cost vs ROI — tabletop tent replacement $30-$300/year per location vs new-customer LTV $300-$15K typical; programme cost rarely material to ROI when conversion drives even modest customer acquisition lift.

faq.question: What matters most for a tabletop review prompt?
faq.answer: Placement and clarity usually matter most, because the prompt often has to work without staff explanation and must attract attention on its own.

faq.question: Should a tabletop prompt always be a rigid card?
faq.answer: Not always. A rigid card can feel more premium, but a sticker or integrated stand can be better when the surface, cleaning routine or available space changes the practical fit.

faq.question: Which tabletop tent form factor works best — A-frame, prism, lucite holder, or engraved block?
faq.answer: Match the form to the venue gravitas + cleaning regime + placement context. Bi-fold A-frame tent (6×4×6 in cardstock, $0.30-$1.00) is most common for restaurant + cafe + casual venues; freestanding + cost-effective. Tri-fold prism tent (3-sided, $0.40-$1.20) for round tables + central placement visible from all sides. Tabletop stand with insert pocket (lucite/acrylic/wood holder + replaceable paper insert, $3-$15 per stand + $0.20 per refresh) for reusable + cleaning-resistant + premium feel. Lucite counter-block (3×3×3 in acrylic block with engraved 'Tap to Review', $5-$20) for minimalist + counter-only venues. Engraved wooden block ($8-$30, FSC hardwood) for premium restaurant + spa + coffee with sustainability emphasis. Metal tabletop sign ($15-$50, brass / brushed steel) for luxury restaurant + premium hotel + private dining. Window decal + countertop sticker ($0.30-$0.80) for venues without tabletop space.

faq.question: Where should we place tabletop prompts across different venues?
faq.answer: Match placement to customer-flow + exposure window. Restaurant table center A-frame (10-25% sustained tap rate at casual + family-style). Restaurant check-presenter slot (8-15% at full-service). Cafe / coffee shop tabletop (5-10% at fast turnover). Hotel in-room desk / nightstand (3-10% with multi-day exposure). Hotel lobby seating (2-5% passive). Spa / salon waiting area magazine table (3-8% during 5-15 min wait). Medical clinic exam room counter (4-10% HIPAA-compliant generic prompt). Medical waiting room reading table (3-8% during longer waits). Bar / lounge top (5-12% with signature drink card adjacent). Boutique fitting room exit (4-10%). B2B conference room + reception (3-8%). Veterinary exam room (5-12% with pet imagery). Visibility hierarchy: at-eye-level when seated (best); 45-degree angle when standing (acceptable); flat on table (lowest); freestanding A-frame outperforms flat by 3-5× tap-rate.

Replacement reserve 5-15% per year for damage / wear / loss / theft (higher in restaurant + bar than spa + clinic). Per-location count: small venue 5-15 tents; mid-size restaurant / spa 20-50 tents; large hotel / coffee chain location 50-200 tents. Multi-location chain (50-5,000 locations × 20-50 tents) = 1K-250K tents at scale. Procurement leverage: corporate bulk procurement (10K-1M+ tents annually) yields $0.15-$0.60 per tent at scale; multi-year + cross-brand contract 10-20% discount. Brand-refresh trigger drives full-estate reorder 12-18 months typical. SKU consolidation: 3-5 strategic tent designs covering 90% of placements (casual A-frame + premium folded card + reusable lucite holder + counter sticker + premium wood/metal). Reference deployments: Cava Group, Chipotle, Sweetgreen, Shake Shack, Starbucks, Marriott Bonvoy lobby tents, Hilton Honors lobby tents.
